cabinet.name: Kabinet-Jetten
cabinet.type: Minority coalition cabinet of D66, VVD and CDA

coalition_agreement.title_nl: Aan de slag. Bouwen aan een beter Nederland
coalition_agreement.title_en: Getting to work. Building a better Netherlands

cabinet.summary: The Jetten cabinet is a minority cabinet: D66 (26), VVD (22) and CDA (18) hold 66 of 150 seats in the House of Representatives and 22 of 75 seats in the Senate, so it needs support from one or more opposition groups for every proposal in both chambers. Parlement.com describes it as the first true minority cabinet since 1945. The coalition agreement states that the cabinet will invite both coalition and opposition MPs to contribute early. On 12 November 2026 the tax plan for 2027 passed the House by 76 votes to 74 after D66 and CDA agreed an amendment with PRO and Volt, while coalition party VVD voted against. After crisis talks, Prime Minister Jetten informed the House on 17 November 2026 that the coalition continues in the same composition; NOS reported that future support is to be sought from 'a bloc of parties', with no choice made yet.

coalition_agreement_points.text: The agreement calls solving the housing shortage its top priority and refers to a desired production of 100,000 homes per year. In new regional housing deals the aim is that two-thirds of homes are affordable, of which 30% social rent and 25% affordable owner-occupied. NOS reports 1 billion euros per year from 2029 for building affordable homes.

Objection procedures are cut back: one stage of appeal, fixed deadlines for rulings, higher thresholds for objection and appeal. An annual Simplification Act is to make adding storeys and splitting homes easier, permit-free where possible. Permanent residence in holiday homes is to be allowed.

Social housing tenants get an annual income test to determine whether the rent is still appropriate, and new social tenants a wealth test. The tax treatment of the owner-occupied home (including mortgage interest deduction) stays unchanged. The transfer tax on homes not lived in by the buyer goes from 8% to 7% from 2027.

A 'freedom contribution' (vrijheidsbijdrage) for security is raised through taxes: via income tax 1.5 billion euros in 2027 and 3.4 billion per year from 2028, and via a higher employer disability-fund premium 1.5 billion in 2027 and 1.7 billion per year from 2028. Corporate income tax is not raised; the expat scheme, the business succession scheme and the innovation box are kept.

The new box 3 system based on actual returns is to be developed further into a capital gains system. An EU investment account is introduced and a 'win-win loan' is studied. From 2028 the asset limits for healthcare benefit are set equal to the tax-free allowance in box 3.

The Netherlands is to take a leading role with other European countries in modernising international refugee law, with the stated aim that asylum applications are eventually submitted and processed outside Europe. The agreement supports the EU return regulation and closed reception at the external border for applications with little chance of success under the EU migration pact.

The Asylum Emergency Measures Act and the Two-Status System Act are implemented in full if adopted by the Senate. If applications rise sharply and unexpectedly, extra measures follow, possibly a temporary emergency stop on family reunification for people with subsidiary protection. The asylum procedure is simplified; emergency reception in hotels and cruise ships is replaced by regular places. The dispersal act (spreidingswet) stays in force for now.

The advice of the Roemer committee and of the Social and Economic Council is implemented against rogue temp agencies; employers get more responsibility for housing; bans on agency work can be imposed in sectors with persistent abuses. A three-year pilot brings skilled workers to defined sectors under conditions including a salary requirement and a housing requirement. Asylum seekers with a good chance of a permit may work after three months.

Tackling grid congestion is given 'highest priority'; a Grid Congestion Crisis Act is to speed up permit procedures. Offshore wind is supported through contracts for difference for 40 GW; the SDE++ subsidy gets 6 new rounds (through 2032, 8 billion euros per year according to SRA); work continues on building at least four new nuclear power plants, which can be conventional or small modular reactors.

The agreement backs electrification of industry, CO2 storage under the North Sea, green gas and green hydrogen, and heat networks. According to Parlement.com's summary the 2030 climate target is kept, the Groningen gas field stays closed and there is no gas extraction in the Wadden Sea.

Nitrogen targets for 2035 are laid down in law per sector, relative to 2019: 42%-46% (ammonia) for agriculture, 50% (ammonia) for industry and 50% (nitrogen oxides) for mobility, with a 2030 target range of 23-25% for agriculture. The critical deposition value is to be replaced 'as soon as possible' by a legally tenable alternative. If the 2035 target is missed, animal or phosphate rights of farms are cut 'as an ultimate remedy'.

20 billion euros is set aside for agriculture, nature and nitrogen, including voluntary closure of livestock farms. Voluntary buy-out schemes continue, focused on farms near overburdened Natura 2000 areas. A land-based farming standard is introduced by 2032 at the latest; animal and phosphate rights are extended to calves and goats.

The compulsory deductible (eigen risico) is indexed and raised by 60 euros in 2027; NOS reports a rise from 385 to 460 euros. A maximum of 150 euros per treatment applies (from 2028, in specialist medical care, according to SRA). The tax deduction for specific care costs ends in 2028 (618 million euros per year according to NOS); home help becomes income-dependent; a sugar tax and free school fruit are announced.

Defence spending is scaled up to the NATO norm of 3.5% of GDP, which is to be anchored in law. The armed forces are to grow to at least 122,000 people; a compulsory survey for young people is introduced as a first step, with reintroduction of selective compulsory attendance considered if results fall short. NOS reports 19 billion euros extra for defence.

Multi-year military and financial support for Ukraine continues and the Netherlands argues for using frozen Russian assets. The agreement invests in development cooperation as 'a step towards the international OECD norm'. Parlement.com's summary lists abolishing unanimity in EU foreign policy and a simpler Article 7 procedure among the EU positions.

The WW benefit becomes higher at the start and is shortened to one year. According to SRA: maximum duration one year from 2028; from 2030 a benefit of 80% in the first two months and stricter entitlement rules; the maximum daily wage is lowered by 20% from 2029.

The cabinet 'works on proposals' to make continued payment of wages during illness more workable for employers, especially small and medium-sized businesses; the agreement gives no figures. The IVA benefit (for full and permanent disability) is abolished for new cases (from 2030 according to SRA). Compensation of employers for the transition payment after two years of illness is abolished.

From 1 January 2033 the state pension age is linked directly to the rise in life expectancy (one-to-one according to SRA; nearly 3 billion euros per year according to NOS). Tax support for supplementary pensions of the highest incomes is reduced over six years; SRA reports the maximum pensionable salary is frozen at 137,800 euros from 2027 through 2032.

A legal presumption of employment is introduced and a Self-Employed Persons Act (Zelfstandigenwet) replaces part of an earlier bill. Nearly free childcare for working parents continues unchanged, with abolition of the childcare benefit through direct financing. A statutory internship allowance is announced.

NOS reports 1 billion euros extra for education next year, rising to 1.5 billion, the scrapping of earlier education cuts and a higher grant for students living away from home. The cabinet works towards the norm of 3% of GDP for research and development spending and expands the WBSO tax credit for AI and technology.

A National Investment Institution is set up for loans and venture capital the market does not provide. Each year at least 500 rules are to be scrapped or simplified. NOS reports a target of 1.5% economic growth.

The budget annex states that the deficit at the end of the cabinet period comes out at 2.1% of GDP (ex ante, Miljoenennota 2026 baseline). Structural windfalls may, under conditions, be used one-third for tax relief, one-third for investment and one-third for debt repayment. The Netherlands keeps to the EU Stability and Growth Pact; a proposal to extend the budget horizon to 8 years is worked out.

The agreement announces reform of the electoral system for the Senate, a right for the Senate to send bills back, a study of an electoral threshold and of a new electoral system for the House in which preference votes weigh more, and a comprehensive act on political parties. Parlement.com's summary also lists constitutional review by courts and a lobby register.

The chapter on cooperation states that the cabinet needs broader support in both chambers than the three parties provide, will invite coalition and opposition MPs to contribute early, and wants to restore consultation with civil society organisations ('the polder') and with municipalities and provinces.

formation_timeline.event: The Schoof cabinet (PVV, VVD, NSC, BBB) falls: the PVV leaves the coalition after the other parties refuse additional asylum measures beyond the coalition agreement; Prime Minister Schoof offers the cabinet's resignation and it continues as a caretaker (demissionary) cabinet.
The House debates the resignation of the Schoof cabinet.
Replacements for the departed PVV ministers and state secretaries are in place.

Foreign minister Caspar Veldkamp (NSC) resigns because he felt he could not take enough measures against Israel over the situation in Gaza; the other NSC ministers and state secretaries leave the same day.
New VVD and BBB ministers and state secretaries are sworn in to fill the NSC posts.
Early election for the House of Representatives. D66 and PVV each win 26 seats; D66 becomes the largest party by 29,668 votes. Turnout is 78.3%.
The party leaders designate Wouter Koolmees (D66) as scout (verkenner).
The Electoral Council (Kiesraad) hands over the official result.
The newly elected House is sworn in.
After a debate on the scout's report the House appoints Hans Wijers (D66) and Sybrand Buma (CDA) as informateurs.
Hans Wijers withdraws as informateur one day after his appointment; Buma continues alone.
Thom van Campen (VVD) is elected Speaker of the House in the third round, with 79 of 148 valid votes.
Informateur Buma hands over his final report.
The House debates Buma's report and appoints Rianne Letschert (D66) as informateur.
Letschert, D66, VVD and CDA opt for a minority cabinet without other parties.
Seven of the 26 PVV members of the House leave the group after criticising leader Geert Wilders' course and form Groep Markuszower; the PVV keeps 19 seats.
D66, VVD and CDA present the coalition agreement 'Aan de slag. Bouwen aan een beter Nederland'; informateur Letschert delivers her final report.
The House debates the agreement and appoints Rob Jetten (D66) as formateur.
Nathalie van Berkel (D66) withdraws as intended State Secretary for Finance; on 19 February Eelco Eerenberg is named in her place.
The Jetten cabinet (D66, VVD, CDA; 18 ministers and 10 state secretaries) is sworn in by the King at Huis ten Bosch Palace, 117 days after the election.
Mona Keijzer leaves the BBB group and continues as an independent member (Lid Keijzer), after the group chose Henk Vermeer to succeed Caroline van der Plas as leader.
Prime Minister Jetten delivers the government statement (regeringsverklaring) in the House; the debate runs on 25 and 26 February.
Municipal elections in 340 of 342 municipalities. Turnout is 53.75%. Local parties together receive 33.41% of the votes; the joint GL/PvdA lists 11.77%, VVD 11.62%, CDA 11.13%, D66 9.30%.
The Senate adopts the act introducing a two-status asylum system, which distinguishes refugees from people with subsidiary protection and tightens family reunification.
The Senate approves the act implementing the EU Asylum and Migration Pact.

Energy crisis (no exact date given in the source): because of disruptions related to the Middle East and Iran the cabinet moves to phase 1 of the national oil crisis plan and releases nearly one billion euros in support measures.
The cabinet presents a package to address the nitrogen problem, with 20 billion euros for the transition of farming and nature restoration.

The House presidium allows the GroenLinks-PvdA group to be called Progressief Nederland (PRO), ahead of a founding congress scheduled for 13 June; Groep Markuszower may not use the name of its new party, De Nederlandse Alliantie, in the House.
Sybrand van Haersma Buma becomes vice-president of the Council of State.

Prinsjesdag (Budget Day): the King's Speech is delivered and finance minister Heinen presents the Miljoenennota 2027, which projects expenditure of 516.8 billion euros, revenue of 481.2 billion and a deficit of 2.9% of GDP in 2027.
The cabinet reallocates infrastructure funds, giving priority to maintenance (18 billion euros), which delays some construction projects.
Minister Van Essen submits a bill replacing targets based on the critical deposition value with statutory emission targets.

The House adopts an amendment by PRO and Volt, agreed with D66 and CDA, shifting about 1 billion euros in taxes from labour to capital, and passes the Belastingplan 2027 (tax plan) by 76 votes to 74; coalition party VVD votes against.
Crisis meeting of the coalition; VVD leader and deputy prime minister Yeşilgöz calls the minority cabinet a 'failed experiment' ('mislukt experiment'). Talks continue on 15 and 16 November.

Jetten informs the House that the coalition continues in the same composition and that Council of State vice-president Buma is asked to advise on structural agreements between cabinet and House on a financial framework for budget decisions.

upcoming.event: Advice by Council of State vice-president Sybrand van Haersma Buma on a financial framework and procedural rules for cooperation between cabinet and House; Parlement.com reports he was asked on 17 November 2026 to advise within a month.
Elections for the Provincial Councils (Provinciale Staten) and the electoral colleges, and on the same day for the 21 water boards.
Candidate nomination day for the Senate election.
Senate election: the members of the Provincial Councils and the electoral colleges elect all 75 senators.
The sitting senators leave and the new Senate is installed.
Prinsjesdag 2027 (Budget Day falls on the third Tuesday of September): King's Speech and presentation of the 2028 budget.
